blocks.text: (Screengrab from Senate of the Philippines / YouTube) MANILA, Philippines — Several senators on Tuesday pressed the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) over the reported agreement requiring the Philippines to source 100 percent of its agricultural and energy imports from the United States. During the Senate’s deliberations on the proposed 2027 budget for the DFA, Sen. Imee Marcos asked whether the DFA had prior knowledge of the supposed arrangement between US President Donald Trump and Pres. Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. during their bilateral talk last Nov. 18.
